# recv.fund documentation

> Documentation for recv.fund, self-hosted, non-custodial stablecoin payment software for Solana and Robinhood Chain. Merchants run the server; funds settle to a wallet they register on-chain.

Use the merchant installation origin for API requests. Inspect its /api/v1/integration/capabilities and /api-json. Project keys use API-Key; never use a dashboard JWT or installation admin key in its place. Never send credentials to docs.recv.fund.

## Start here

- [AI agent workflow](https://docs.recv.fund/agents/index.md): Setup, payments, verification and permissions.
- [Complete documentation](https://docs.recv.fund/llms-full.txt): All pages in one text file.

## Introduction

- [Welcome](https://docs.recv.fund/index.md): What recv.fund is, what runs on your server, what never leaves your control, and the chains and tokens supported at launch.
- [What's new](https://docs.recv.fund/whats-new.md): Release notes for recv.fund, newest first.
- [Use cases](https://docs.recv.fund/use-cases.md): Who recv.fund is built for and what each kind of business gets from it.

## Deployment guide

- [Introduction](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/introduction.md): Three ways to run recv.fund on your own server - the one-line script, a docker compose project you write by hand, or a build from source - and what the server needs.
- [Quick setup](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/quick-setup.md): Install recv.fund with the one-line script, with every prompt and its default.
- [Advanced setup](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/advanced-setup.md): The compose project the installer writes, every environment variable, volumes, external Postgres, running behind your own proxy, and updating by hand.
- [Script usage](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/script-usage.md): Every flag of the recv.fund install script, with what it does and its default.

## Onboarding guide

- [Introduction](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/introduction.md): What onboarding covers, the order of the steps, what you need before you start, and what an installation needs before it can accept a payment.
- [Root account setup](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/root-account-setup.md): The signup page that creates the owner account and first project, signing in, changing passwords, the first installation settings, and inviting teammates.
- [Node configuration](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/node-configuration.md): The Nodes page - the recv.fund deployment the installation connects to on each network, the fee for new registrations, the RPC node pool with preferred, active and public flags, connection tests, processing cursors and the currency catalog.
- [Hot wallet](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/hot-wallet.md): The one private key the server holds - generating or importing it, how it is stored, assigning it to projects, reading balances, funding it, and what it pays for.
- [Merchant registration](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/merchant-registration.md): Registering a project on-chain from the Registrations page - connecting a browser wallet, choosing the cold wallet (settlement address), signing the single registration transaction, the fee fixed for the registration, confirming it on the server, and what changes afterwards.
- [Test payment](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/test-payment.md): Creating a customer and a payment link in the dashboard, what the customer sees on the checkout page, how the payment is credited and confirmed, and what the dashboard shows.
- [Funds sweeping](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/funds-sweeping.md): How deposit balances reach the settlement wallet - the activation threshold, the amount, address-count and time triggers, manual sweeps on the Sweeps page, the fee taken at sweep, what the hot wallet pays, and what a sweep does to the deposit account.

## Features

- [Features](https://docs.recv.fund/features/index.md): What the recv.fund dashboard, checkout page and API do, with one page per feature.
- [Payment links](https://docs.recv.fund/features/payment-links.md): Creating payments from the dashboard or the API, what a payment carries, its states, the checkout page the customer sees, partial and over payment, expiry, history and CSV export.
- [Customer deposit wallets](https://docs.recv.fund/features/customer-deposit-wallets.md): Permanent per-customer deposit addresses derived from your on-chain merchant registration, how deposits are found and credited, unmatched deposits, missed-payment rechecks and customer history.
- [Projects](https://docs.recv.fund/features/multi-brand-projects.md): One install, several brands. Each project has its own branding, enabled currencies, payout policy, API keys, webhook endpoints, hot wallet assignment and team membership.
- [API keys](https://docs.recv.fund/features/api-keys.md): Project API keys on the Developers page, the API-Key header, what a key can reach, revocation and the per-key rate limit.
- [User management](https://docs.recv.fund/features/user-management.md): The five roles, inviting members with a temporary password, forced password change, deactivation, session revocation and the activity log.
- [Analytics](https://docs.recv.fund/features/analytics.md): The overview page: confirmed receipts in USD, date presets and custom ranges, receipts by project and by network or currency, first-time and returning payers.
- [Payouts](https://docs.recv.fund/features/payouts.md): Sending funds from the hot wallet: the address book, creating a payout, approval by email one-time code, USD minimum and limits, durable execution, states and payout webhooks.
- [Sweeps](https://docs.recv.fund/features/sweeps.md): Moving customer deposit balances to your settlement wallet: activation threshold, amount, count and time triggers, automatic scheduling, manual sweeps, the fee at sweep, execution and bookkeeping.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.recv.fund/features/webhooks.md): Endpoints per project, the X-Recv-Signature and X-Payram-Signature headers, HMAC verification, the retry schedule, the delivery log and the SEND_WEBHOOKS switch.
- [Operator mode](https://docs.recv.fund/features/operator-mode.md): Operator mode, one install serving several merchants with a markup, is planned and not part of this release. What one install can do today.

## API integration

- [Introduction](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/introduction.md): Base URL, the API-Key header, rate limits, idempotency, test mode, reference ids, the end-to-end payment flow and what is and is not compatible with PayRam.
- [Overview](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/index.md): The four payment endpoints and the payment webhook, what each one does and when to call it.
- [Checkout endpoints](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/checkout-endpoints.md): The public endpoints behind the hosted checkout page, keyed by reference id, for merchants who build their own checkout: read, select a currency, prepare a wallet transaction, confirm a hash.
- [Payouts API](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payouts-api.md): Create, read and list payouts from the project's hot wallet with the API key, how approval and idempotency work, and the payout webhook events.
- [Create payment](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/create-payment.md): POST /api/v1/payment creates a payment for a customer and returns its reference id and checkout URL.
- [Deposit options](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/deposit-options.md): GET /api/v1/blockchain-currency/reference/{reference_id} lists every currency the customer may pay with and the deposit address already assigned on each chain.
- [Assign deposit address](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/assign-deposit-address.md): POST /api/v1/deposit-address/reference/{reference_id} derives the customer's permanent deposit address on a chain and selects that chain for the payment.
- [Payment status](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/payment-status.md): GET /api/v1/payment/reference/{reference_id} returns the state, amounts, deposit address and confirmation progress of a payment.
- [Payment webhook](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/webhook.md): Event names, payload fields, the X-Recv-Signature and X-Payram-Signature headers, how to verify the HMAC, the retry schedule and how to handle deliveries idempotently.
- [Ticker](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/ticker.md): GET /api/v1/ticker: every active currency on the installation's network with its current USD price.

## Support

- [Glossary](https://docs.recv.fund/support/glossary.md): Terms as recv.fund uses them in the dashboard, the API, the on-chain program and contracts, and this documentation.
- [Networks and tokens](https://docs.recv.fund/support/networks.md): The chains, networks, RPC endpoints, explorers, tokens, decimals and confirmation defaults an install ships with.
- [Links](https://docs.recv.fund/support/links.md): The recv.fund sites, the installer, chain explorers, RPC endpoints, token references and how to contact the team.
- [Change log](https://docs.recv.fund/support/change-log.md): Every recv.fund release, newest first, with what it includes and what it does not.
- [FAQ](https://docs.recv.fund/support/faq.md): Answers on custody, fees, downtime, keys, wallets, underpayment, expiry, refunds, testnets, updates, backups and support.

## AI agent guide

- [Integrate with an AI agent](https://docs.recv.fund/agents/index.md): A complete entry point for AI coding assistants integrating, configuring and operating a self-hosted recv.fund installation.
- [Agent installation and setup workflow](https://docs.recv.fund/agents/installation-and-setup.md): An ordered, evidence-based path from a fresh instance to a confirmed test payment and settlement.
- [Agent payment integration workflow](https://docs.recv.fund/agents/payment-integration.md): Exact API examples, signed webhook verification, retry boundaries and fulfillment rules for merchant backend integrations.
- [Agent verification and recovery](https://docs.recv.fund/agents/verification-and-recovery.md): Diagnose setup and payment problems with observed server and chain evidence; never fabricate successful verification.
- [Agent security and permissions](https://docs.recv.fund/agents/security-and-permissions.md): Credential boundaries, human authorization for funds, safe contract tooling and release evidence for automated integrations.
